source_title: ‘Star Wars’ Actor Alden Ehrenreich Recalls Bombing His ‘Spider-Man’ Audition: ‘I Blew That Up’ - People.com
source_excerpt:
Andrew Garfield ended up earning the part of Peter Parker a.k.a. Spider-Man
Earl Gibson III/Deadline via Getty; Moviestore/Shutterstock
Alden Ehrenreich revealed on the Happy Sad Confused podcast that he was in the running to play Peter Parker in 2012’s The Amazing Spider-Man
But, he recalled, he “kinda showed up not memorized” and “blew that up”
Andrew Garfield, who Ehrenreich called “one of the best actors of my generation,” was instead cast as Spider-Man
Could Alden Ehrenreich have played Spider-Man? To hear him tell it, the casting was unlikely given his audition.
The Solo: A Star Wars Story actor, 36, was around 21 years old when he found himself in the running to play Peter Parker in 2012’s The Amazing Spider-Man , he told Josh Horowitz recently on Happy Sad Confused .
“I showed up woefully unprepared,” recalled Ehrenreich. “In a way that I would never do later [in my career].”
In fact, said the actor, he “kinda showed up not memorized.”
Andrew Garfield ended up playing Marvel’s iconic Spider-Man in three films from 2012 to 2021. “I’m not suggesting that I would’ve gotten the role,” Ehrenreich said. “I think Andrew Garfield is one of the best actors of my generation, easily, he’s incredible, and I’m sure he would’ve gotten it anyway.”
The audition, continued the Weapons star, involved “a full set” and “10 actors having dinner” who were, unlike him, “off-book.”
“And so if I did have a chance for that, then I think I blew that up,” Ehrenreich said.
Plus, he admitted, he wasn’t enthused about playing the webbed hero anyway. “All that existed at that time was the Tobey Maguire [ Spider-Man movies], and it seemed like it was the same story,” recalled Ehrenreich.
“I also just felt that it wasn’t my role and it wasn’t right for me,” he said. “I don’t know. I, in that moment, really didn’t wanna do it, to be honest.”

Ultimately, it was for the best. He added, “Getting really famous at 22 would’ve been a bad idea… I’ve been very lucky that it’s been very gradual over the years.”
Ehrenreich’s career has indeed been on the rise — and has included a superhero franchise, as he appeared in episodes of Disney+ series Ironheart in 2025. This June, he won a Tony Award for his Broadway debut in the Gina Gionfriddo play Becky Shaw .
He now stars opposite Helen Mirren in A Talent for Murder , in theaters now.
